name: Boredoms
label: Warner Bros.
lede: Eye's other band drove an excavator through a club wall. Boredoms took that appetite to Warner Bros., the Lollapalooza main stage and sunset drum rituals for 77, 88 and 111 players.

eras.title: Osaka noise kids with a bad name
eras.text: Before Boredoms, Yamantaka Eye fronted Hanatarash, an Osaka noise act that, per Wikipedia, once drove an excavator through a venue's back wall onto the stage. Most clubs banned them. Boredoms began as the punk band next door and soon had a reputation of its own.

years.h: Eye leaves Hanatarash's wreckage for a punk band
years.p: Yamantaka Eye starts Acid Makki & Combi and Zombie in Osaka with Hanatarash drummer Ikuo Taketani, guitarist Tabata Mitsuru, bassist Hosoi Hisato and singer Makki Sasarato. Their first recording, U.S.A., lands on a compilation tape.
years.xp:
Hanatarash, Eye's other band, was billed as a noise and performance-art act whose shows were, per Wikipedia, built around on-stage destruction. Wikipedia records Eye cutting a dead cat in half with a machete, and strapping a circular saw to his back and almost cutting his leg off.

The band was quickly banned from most venues, which is the reputation Boredoms started out next to.

years.h: Buzzcocks hand the band a name
years.p: Makki Sasarato leaves, Yoshikawa Toyohito takes the drums and Hira the bass, and the band becomes Boredoms, after the [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] song Boredom.

years.h: Anal by Anal goes out as the first EP
years.p: Eye and Tabata Mitsuru cut Boredoms' first official release. The title tells you what kind of band this was.

years.h: Tabata quits for Zeni Geva, and Yamamoto takes the guitar
years.p: Tabata Mitsuru leaves for [[Zeni Geva|4a48f534-9b66-495c-a934-b775beda1ca7]]. [[Seiichi Yamamoto|d35596ac-7786-4f50-abb5-cc4fb501ccb7]] steps into his spot.

years.h: Eye cuts up a first album: Osorezan no Stooges Kyo
years.p: Harsh, dissonant punk that Eye chopped and re-edited in the studio, with nods to [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Funkadelic|cf042013-3edd-46c4-9b0e-a62faac98d0b]].

years.h: Yoshimi P-We, from Eye's UFO or Die, takes over drums
years.p: Unhappy with Yoshikawa Toyohito, the band recruits [[Yoshimi P-We|fa119f2e-f1a1-4f3a-bd12-900d43ba7ce3]], the first woman in Boredoms. Yoshikawa shifts to percussion, then leaves.

eras.title: A major label's strangest signing
eras.text: Sonic Youth and John Zorn carried Boredoms to America, and Warner Bros. signed them. What followed was some of the strangest music a major has issued, tours with Sonic Youth and Nirvana, and a Lollapalooza main stage.

years.h: Soul Discharge crosses the Pacific
years.p: The second album gets a US release, and Boredoms land deals with Warner in Japan and its Reprise imprint in America.

years.h: Eye sings for Zorn's Naked City
years.p: Eye guests on vocals with [[John Zorn|7ec4a553-73e5-4c0d-a071-a82b83a309e6]]'s [[Naked City|fc4dea85-3998-4130-a56e-907689160480]] and befriends Sonic Youth. Wikipedia counts both among the band's ties to New York's downtown scene.

years.h: Chew Hasegawa fills in, then ATR takes the second drum seat
years.p: Kazuya Nishimura, known as ATR, settles in beside Yoshimi P-We after Hasegawa's brief stint.

years.h: Pop Tatari goes out on Warner and baffles everyone
years.p: Wikipedia notes it is generally seen as one of the strangest albums a major label ever released. The band tours with Sonic Youth.

years.h: Eye and Sonic Youth make TV Shit
years.p: Eye records the EP with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] for [[Thurston Moore|8ba48525-d922-42ee-9775-97b7b8f9712e]]'s Ecstatic Peace label. With Zorn, as Mystic Fugu Orchestra, he also makes the first release on Zorn's Tzadik.

years.cap: Boredoms at Soma, San Diego, May 1993
years.h: Eight straight nights opening for Nirvana
years.p: From late October into early November 1993, Boredoms support [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]] for eight consecutive shows. They also tour with grindcore band [[Brutal Truth|4ddc0620-38e2-40ec-8915-009967520168]] that year.

years.h: Chocolate Synthesizer sells well for a band this odd
years.p: The Reprise album did better than an experimental record has any right to, per Wikipedia. Alternative Press later ranked it among the best albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Boredoms land the Lollapalooza main stage
years.p: At the height of their US profile, they play the 1994 tour's main stage behind the just-released Chocolate Synthesizer.

yt: Live at Pine Street Theatre, Portland, June 1994
years.h: EDA arrives through Pavement, and Reprise walks
years.p: Percussionist EDA joins after an introduction from [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] bassist [[Mark Ibold|003db9eb-2a01-4ece-a5e0-87000aa502d7]]. The same year Reprise drops Boredoms.

eras.title: Orbit, then silence
eras.text: The noise didn't stop, it went into orbit. By the late '90s the band was making long, drum-heavy psychedelic jams that critics tied to Can and krautrock, and Vision Creation Newsun is often called the peak. After a remix series, they vanished for years.

years.h: Super æ swaps Japanoise for long jams
years.p: After the Super Go!!!!!! EP, Boredoms stretch out into psychedelic drum-heavy jams. Pitchfork put it on its list of the top 100 albums of the 1990s.

years.h: Vision Creation Newsun, the one fans point to
years.p: Multi-drum tribal grooves, cosmic synths and bursts of noise, out in Japan in 1999. Wikipedia says it is often considered the band's greatest achievement.

years.h: Eye draws the cover of Beck's Midnite Vultures
years.p: The artist behind most Boredoms sleeves also did art for [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]]'s Midnite Vultures, the Sexx Laws single and the Stray Blues B-sides set.

years.h: Eye hands the catalog to guest DJs, then goes quiet
years.p: He oversees a series of guest-DJ remix albums, releasing his own, Rebore, vol. 0, in 2000. After that, no records and no tours for years.

years.h: A Flaming Lips album takes Yoshimi's name
years.p: While Boredoms sit idle, [[The Flaming Lips|1f43d76f-8edf-44f6-aaf1-b65f05ad9402]] release Yoshimi Battles the Pink Robots. Yoshimi plays on it, and Wayne Coyne said she inspired it.

eras.title: Three drummers and an infinity sign
eras.text: The rumored breakup wasn't one. A slimmed-down band returned as V∞redoms with three drummers and a synthesizer, left Warner for the small Japanese label Commmons, and found Thrill Jockey for the rest of the world.

years.h: Boredoms come back as V∞redoms
years.p: Eye, Yoshimi, ATR, EDA and synth player Izumi Kiyoshi resurface with three drummers. The band signs with Vice Records in the US.

years.cap: Yamantaka Eye at All Tomorrow's Parties, 2004
years.h: Four years on, Seadrum/House of Sun
years.p: Mostly recorded before the hiatus, it moves the band from WEA Japan to the small label Commmons. Reviews were mostly positive: 73 on Metacritic.

years.h: Christmas Eve 2004 becomes Super Roots 9
years.p: The December 24 concert is recorded and released in 2007, the first Super Roots record since 1999.

years.cap: Boredoms at the Intonation festival, Chicago
years.h: EDA goes to Adrena Adrena; Yojiro Tatekawa fills in
years.p: EDA quits to start an audio-visual project with artist Daisy Dickinson. Yojiro Tatekawa takes the drum seat, and ATR is gone too.

years.h: Sonic Youth take V∞redoms to Japan for three dates
years.p: Billed as V∞redoms, the band plays three shows with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], Pitchfork reported.

years.h: At 7:07 pm on 7/7/07, 77 drummers fill Brooklyn
years.p: Boredoms lead 77 drummers at the Empire-Fulton Ferry section of Brooklyn Bridge Park, with Yoshimi P-We as drummer one.
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, Eye chose 77 after counting 77 steps up the Temple of the Sun at Palenque in Mexico. Drummer Muneomi Senju sat in with the band.

The event became a template the band repeated in 2008, 2009 and 2011, each on a matching date.

eras.title: Counting drummers, one date at a time
eras.text: With Thrill Jockey handling them outside Japan, Boredoms turned the Boadrum into a traveling ritual: 88 drummers at the La Brea Tar Pits, nine at Terminal 5, 111 on an Australian beach. Eye added a seven-necked guitar and motion sensors.

years.h: Tiny Mix Tapes breaks the Thrill Jockey signing
years.p: The site's headline declares Thrill Jockey is fucking awesome. The label handles Boredoms outside Japan from here.

years.h: Eye straps on a seven-necked guitar for the Iron & Wine tour
years.p: On a 2008 US tour with [[Iron & Wine|c3f28da8-662d-4f09-bdc7-3084bf685930]], Yamantaka Eye plays a new instrument called the Sevena, or Sevener.

years.h: 88 drummers, 88 minutes, 8:08 pm at the La Brea Tar Pits
years.p: On 8/8/08 Boredoms lead 88 drummers in Los Angeles. A second 88 Boadrum in Brooklyn is conducted by [[Gang Gang Dance|83f1cb07-1745-48e6-8576-428604e67aa8]].
years.xp: Pitchfork's headline on the announcement was that Nike was bringing 88 Boadrum to LA and Brooklyn, and Rolling Stone covered the band's taste for rhythm and numerology that August.

years.h: Super Roots 10 is the next in the EP series
years.p: Another installment in Boredoms' long-running Super Roots series.

years.h: Nine drummers at Terminal 5, 9:09 pm on 9/9/09
years.p: Yoshimi and Yojiro Tatekawa play with seven guests in Manhattan, among them [[Zach Hill|df6a1106-6caf-465b-bcfd-0b80d2b53516]] of [[Hella|1ecbc7e5-6e33-4062-997d-abc550dd63e6]] and Kid Millions of [[Oneida|33c5f321-37b5-4c8e-8eff-a8a6a5ac2e44]].

years.h: Matt Groening's ATP gets two Boadrums
years.p: Boredoms play two Boadrum sets at the festival Matt Groening curates at Butlins in Minehead, then tour London, Japan, Mexico and Melbourne.

years.h: Six drummers circle Eye, and Masuko joins the band
years.p: At ATP's I'll Be Your Mirror in Tokyo, Eye triggers drones by Shinji Masuko with motion sensors while six drummers surround him. Masuko becomes a full member.

years.h: 111 Boadrum closes the count at Byron Bay
years.p: At 11:11 am on 11/11/11, 11 drummers and 100 cymbal players, 111 performers in all, play in Australia. It is the last numbered Boadrum.

years.h: Jeff Mangum picks them: 14 guitarists and six drummers
years.p: [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s [[Jeff Mangum|6a7b9d5e-a863-4a90-a056-77942e9f43de]] books Boredoms for his All Tomorrow's Parties in Minehead, and they play twice.

years.h: 88 cymbal players ring the Barbican
years.p: Boredoms play London's Barbican as part of Doug Aitken's Station to Station: A 30-Day Happening, surrounded by 88 percussionists on cymbals.
